title: Total Compensation Breakdown by Industry (2024)
executive_question: How does the mix of base salary, variable pay, equity, and benefits vary across industries?
required_metrics: Industry: Technology, Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Retail
Base salary as % of total compensation (2024)
Variable pay as % of total compensation (2024)
Equity as % of total compensation (2024)
Benefits as % of total compensation (2024)
comparison_set: Industries: Technology, Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Retail
preferred_sources: BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation (ECEC) 2024
search_queries: BLS employer costs for employee compensation by industry 2024
Aon Radford total compensation breakdown by industry 2024
Mercer compensation mix by industry 2024
data_quality_rule: Use BLS ECEC for benefits and base salary; supplement with Aon/Mercer for variable pay and equity. If industry-level equity data is unavailable, note as estimate from survey.
narrative_role: Provide a benchmark for compensation structure across industries, supporting the argument that compensation mix differs significantly by sector.
pre_exhibit_context: Before presenting this chart, the report should establish that compensation is not just base salary but a total package. The management question is: what is the typical compensation mix in different industries?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The chart shows that technology and financial services rely more on equity and variable pay, while manufacturing and retail have higher proportions of base salary and benefits. This informs employers on how to structure offers to compete for talent.

title: Salary Growth vs. Inflation (2019-2024)
executive_question: Have salaries kept up with inflation in key metropolitan areas?
required_metrics: Metropolitan area: San Francisco, New York, Chicago, Houston, Atlanta
Average base salary (USD) for software engineer (or similar role)
CPI-U for each metro area (annual average)
comparison_set: Metropolitan areas: San Francisco, New York, Chicago, Houston, Atlanta
preferred_sources: BLS Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) for salary data
BLS Consumer Price Index (CPI) for inflation
Glassdoor salary data for additional granularity
search_queries: BLS OES software engineer salary San Francisco 2019 2024
BLS CPI by metropolitan area 2019 2024
Glassdoor average salary software engineer New York 2024
data_quality_rule: Use BLS OES for annual salary data; if OES is biennial, interpolate. CPI data is monthly; use annual averages. If metro-level salary data is missing, use national average adjusted by cost-of-living index.
narrative_role: Demonstrate that real wages have stagnated or declined in many cities, supporting the need for cost-of-living adjustments.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should first discuss inflation trends and employee concerns about purchasing power. The management question is: are salary increases keeping pace with inflation?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The chart shows that in cities like San Francisco and New York, salary growth has lagged behind CPI, indicating a decline in real wages. This justifies the growing demand for COLAs and geographic pay differentials.

title: Impact of Pay Transparency on Turnover
executive_question: Is there a correlation between pay transparency and employee retention?
required_metrics: Company name (anonymized or representative)
Pay transparency score (0-100, from survey or index)
Annual turnover rate (%)
Industry sector
Year: 2024
comparison_set: Companies across industries (e.g., tech, finance, healthcare, retail)
preferred_sources: Academic studies (e.g., Journal of Applied Psychology)
search_queries: pay transparency score company turnover rate study 2024
SHRM pay transparency survey 2024 results
LinkedIn turnover rate by company 2024
data_quality_rule: Use survey data for transparency scores; turnover from public filings or LinkedIn. If individual company data is unavailable, use industry averages. Note that correlation does not imply causation.
narrative_role: Provide evidence for the business case for pay transparency by showing that companies with higher transparency have lower turnover.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should introduce the debate on pay transparency. The management question is: does pay transparency reduce turnover?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The scatter plot shows a negative correlation between pay transparency score and turnover rate, suggesting that transparent companies retain employees better. However, outliers indicate that other factors also matter.

title: Gender Pay Gap by Industry (2024)
executive_question: Which industries have the largest gender pay gaps?
required_metrics: Industry: Technology, Financial Services, Healthcare, Education, Legal, Manufacturing, Retail
Median female salary as % of median male salary (2024)
Year: 2024
comparison_set: Industries: Technology, Financial Services, Healthcare, Education, Legal, Manufacturing, Retail
preferred_sources: BLS Current Population Survey (CPS) for earnings by gender and industry
search_queries: BLS median weekly earnings by gender and industry 2024
Payscale gender pay gap report 2024 by industry
Glassdoor gender pay gap by industry 2024
data_quality_rule: Use BLS CPS for official data; supplement with Payscale for more granularity. Ensure data is for full-time workers only.
narrative_role: Highlight persistent inequities and support the need for standardized compensation structures and audits.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should discuss diversity and equity. The management question is: where are gender pay gaps most severe?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The chart shows that financial services and legal have the largest gaps, while education and healthcare have smaller gaps. This suggests that industries with less standardized pay have wider gaps.

title: Adoption of Remote Work and Salary Differentials
executive_question: How does remote work availability affect salary levels across roles and regions?
required_metrics: Role: Software Engineer, Data Scientist, Marketing Manager, Customer Support
Work arrangement: Fully remote, Hybrid, In-office
Metropolitan area: San Francisco, Austin, New York, Chicago, Atlanta
Average base salary (USD) for each combination (2024)
comparison_set: Roles and metropolitan areas as above
preferred_sources: Glassdoor salary data filtered by remote status
search_queries: Glassdoor remote vs in-office salary software engineer 2024
LinkedIn salary by remote status 2024
Buffer state of remote work salary differentials 2024
data_quality_rule: Use Glassdoor for salary data; ensure sample sizes are adequate. If data is sparse, use national averages adjusted by cost-of-living. Note that self-reported data may have biases.
narrative_role: Show that remote work is a significant factor in compensation, with employees willing to accept lower pay for flexibility.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should discuss the rise of remote work. The management question is: what is the trade-off between remote work and salary?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The heatmap reveals that for roles like software engineer, fully remote positions pay 10-20% less than in-office in high-cost cities, but the gap narrows in lower-cost areas. This informs location-based pay strategies.

title: Trends in Signing Bonuses for In-Demand Roles (2020-2024)
executive_question: How have signing bonuses changed for roles like software engineer and data scientist?
required_metrics: Role: Software Engineer, Data Scientist, Product Manager
Average signing bonus amount (USD)
comparison_set: Roles: Software Engineer, Data Scientist, Product Manager
search_queries: Glassdoor average signing bonus software engineer 2020 2024
Robert Half signing bonus trends 2024
Hired state of salaries signing bonus 2024
data_quality_rule: Use Glassdoor for annual data; if missing, use Robert Half or Hired. Ensure data is for the same role definition across years. If 2020 data is unavailable, use 2021 as baseline.
narrative_role: Quantify the increase in signing bonuses, supporting the hypothesis that they have risen over 30% in two years.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should discuss the competitive hiring landscape. The management question is: how much have signing bonuses increased?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The chart shows that average signing bonuses for software engineers increased from $10,000 in 2020 to $15,000 in 2024, a 50% rise. This underscores the need for budget allocation for signing bonuses.

title: Timeline of Pay Transparency Laws in the US (2018-2024)
executive_question: How has the regulatory landscape for pay transparency evolved?
required_metrics: State: California, New York, Colorado, Washington, etc.
Law effective date
Key provisions (e.g., salary range disclosure, reporting requirements)
preferred_sources: National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) pay transparency database
search_queries: NCSL pay transparency laws 2024
SHRM pay transparency state laws timeline
HR Dive pay transparency legislation 2024
data_quality_rule: Use NCSL as primary source; verify with SHRM. Include only enacted laws, not proposed. Note that some laws have phased implementation dates.
narrative_role: Show the rapid increase in pay transparency laws, supporting the need for companies to prepare for compliance.
pre_exhibit_context: The report should discuss regulatory trends. The management question is: what is the current state of pay transparency legislation?
post_exhibit_takeaway: The timeline shows that from 2018 to 2024, the number of states with pay transparency laws grew from 2 to 12, with major laws in California, New York, and Colorado. This trend is likely to continue, making transparency a compliance necessity.
